picks.reasoning: The Cavaliers are a healthy, heavy favorite, but 9.5 points looks like too many for a game in October. One computer model projects a Cleveland win by about 8, and another puts the Wizards' cover chance near 55% with roughly a 6% edge. Washington is missing Jamir Watkins, Tristan Vukcevic and Justin Champagnie, and AJ Dybantsa is questionable with an ankle injury, so check the injury report before tip-off. This is a small-edge value play on the spread, and Cleveland could easily win by double digits.

picks.event: Detroit Pistons at New York Knicks
picks.reasoning: Detroit is 3-0 and has a strong defense and a strong Cade Cunningham. The Knicks are 0-3 and have struggled to score, and they are still priced as home favorites of about 3.5 to 4 points. The Pistons are short-handed. Jalen Duren is out, and Ausar Thompson and Isaiah Joe are questionable. Those absences are probably already in the line, and a 3-0 start is a small sample. Treat this as a modest-value spread play rather than a strong edge. Check the injury news before tip-off, because a Thompson absence would weaken the case.

Houston closed as only a 1.5-point road favorite when these teams met on Saturday and won 121-114. Monday's line is -5 to -5.5, which looks like a big jump for home court plus VanVleet returning. The market has barely moved, and about 71% of spread tickets are on Houston, which suggests the number leans toward the public side. Atlanta is healthy apart from two minor absences, and the Rockets are thin up front with Adams out and Smart questionable. Early-season samples are small and Houston could still win comfortably, so this is a small edge. Odds are approximate (-110 at -5.0 to -5.5), so check the final number before betting.

picks.reasoning: Denver has the league's second-best defense by opponent rating and is 3-0 on the road. Arizona is 2-4, gives up more touchdowns than any other team, and has lost RB James Conner to injured reserve and traded away WR Marvin Harrison Jr. FPI gives Denver about a 69% win chance and the Squawka model about 79%. Both put the margin at roughly 5 to 9 points, which is above the 4.5 spread. The risk is Denver's offense. Bo Nix has struggled for weeks and the Broncos have been outscored on the season. Several expert picks also lean Arizona, so a close game or an upset is a real possibility.
picks.start_time: 4:05 PM ET (2:05 PM MT / 1:05 PM local in Glendale, AZ)

picks.reasoning: Houston played the Spurs on Oct. 23, so this is the second night of a back-to-back. Reed Sheppard (knee) is out, and Fred VanVleet may also be rested. Atlanta is home and rested, and is 2-0 with a strong defense. Dimers' model puts the Hawks near 58% against a market price of about 50% to 55%. Early-season NBA samples are tiny, and Houston has Sengun and Durant, so the game is close to a toss-up. Odds also vary by book, with Hawks ML listed from -120 to +100, so shop for the best price.

Indiana won 19 games last season and Dallas won 26, yet the Pacers are 6.5-point favorites, and the line has moved from -5.5 to -6.5 since open. Early-season NBA spreads this large tend to overrate small samples, such as Indiana's 1-0 start. Indiana is also missing T.J. McConnell and Johnny Furphy, with Nesmith and Sheppard questionable. Dallas has Cooper Flagg, though Kyrie Irving, Dereck Lively and Santi Aldama are all day-to-day, which could hurt. Dallas lost its opener by 18, and this is a thin-edge play at roughly a coin-flip price, with a real chance the Pacers cover.

picks.event: New England Patriots at Chicago Bears
picks.reasoning: New England is missing both starting guards (Vera-Tucker and Brown), starting CB Carlton Davis and two reserve corners. Right tackle Morgan Moses is also questionable. That is a lot of attrition for a road team on a short week. Chicago is mostly healthy at home, with RG Jonah Jackson cleared to play. Dimers' model gives the Bears about a 62% win probability and a cover edge, while the market has them as only a field-goal favorite. The risks are that a 3-point spread can land exactly on 3, and that New England is 4-2 and has been playing well, so this is a thin edge and not a lock.

This is a near pick'em on opening night, and the market has barely moved. The Heat are only -1.5 at home, and 62% of spread tickets are on Minnesota. Both teams are close to fully healthy. Minnesota's only absence is DiVincenzo, and Goldin is questionable for Miami. Minnesota starts Edwards and LaMelo Ball, so its perimeter shooting should help against a Heat team built around Giannis and Bam inside. Taking the points costs about the same as the moneyline and covers a one-point loss. Opening-night rotations, new rosters and no regular-season sample make this very uncertain, and it is a small edge at best.

The Knicks are the defending champs and open at home, and last season's net rating gap of about 6.5 points favors them by more than this spread. Embiid and James aren't on Philly's first injury report, but Simons is questionable and the new-look Sixers have little chemistry. Josh Hart's ankle is a minor concern, and Mike Brown doesn't expect it to keep him out. Opening-night variance is high and the line has already moved from -3.5 to about -4.5, so this is a small edge. I'd skip it if the number goes past -5.

Jayden Daniels is back at quarterback and 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa is sitting. That makes a 7.5-point spread look a bit high for a Washington team that tied the Giants 27-27 in overtime last week. About 78% of spread bets are on San Francisco, yet the line hasn't moved off -7.5 and the price has shifted slightly toward Washington. The 49ers are unbeaten and cover well (4-1 ATS), and Washington is winless on the road. At -115 the bet needs to win about 53.5% of the time, so the edge is small and this is a modest-value play, not a strong one.

Atlanta is at home and getting points against a Bears team that is thin on defense. Chicago is missing T.J. Edwards and Montez Sweat. Caleb Williams is returning from a torn hamstring after three missed games, so rust is possible. Michael Penix Jr. is expected back from his rib injury, and Atlanta has averaged 34.3 points in his three starts, with Bijan Robinson leading the NFL in rushing yards. Sharp money has reportedly backed Atlanta at +1.5 to +3, and +1.5 is a thin edge. Penix's status and Williams's fitness are both uncertain, and the -110 price is approximate because books differ slightly.

picks.event: Tampa Bay Rays at Cleveland Guardians (ALCS Game 4)
picks.reasoning: Tampa Bay is a 98-win team facing a must-win spot. It has a real starter in Nick Martinez (15-6, 3.10 ERA, rested eight days). Cleveland is expected to use Shawn Armstrong as an opener and then go to a bullpen game. The market has this as nearly a pick'em, so the home-team premium looks small, and the Rays' starting-pitching edge and 5-1 regular-season record against Cleveland aren't fully priced in. Cleveland's bullpen has been excellent and the Guardians lead the series 2-1, so this is a thin edge on a high-variance single game, not a strong lean.

Seattle has the league's top defense in yards allowed per game, and it pressures quarterbacks at a high rate. That matches up well against Bo Nix, who has struggled this season: he has been under 190 passing yards in three of five games and has an 80.8 passer rating. Seattle has also won straight-up after every loss since the start of last season, and Denver is 1-4 against the spread on Thursdays under Sean Payton. The risks are real. -2.5 is a thin margin, Seattle's offensive line has allowed nine sacks and Darnold is under heavy pressure, and Denver's blitz has produced seven takeaways. A low-scoring game could turn on one turnover, so treat this as a small lean.
